desc: The Iberian Struggle depicts the centuries of fractious relationships on the Iberian Peninsula. Though born of the Umayyad Conquest of Iberia in the 8th Century, the Struggle shifts between Phases of hate-fueled violence, wary truces, and pragmatic cooperation. There are few permanent allies in such a situation, and Rulers should be wary of relying purely on a shared Faith or Culture.
name: Iberian Struggle

phases.desc:
After a long period of relatively peaceful coexistence during the Conciliation Phase, complacency begins to set in. Peasantry and nobility alike are comfortable that things just work, allowing more shrewd Characters to take advantage of their naivety.

Eventually, fresh abuses will either cause an escalation into the Hostility Phase, or else savvy politicking reaches an uneasy equilibrium through the Conciliation Phase.

phases.desc:
Tensions flare and tempers fray in this Phase. Repeated acts of malice and escalated misunderstandings during the Opportunity Phase have lead to rising hatred of Characters with differing Cultures, Faiths, or worse: both.

Such bloodshed cannot persist forever, though. Eventually, either cooler heads or simple exhaustion bring the peninsula to the Compromise Phase.

phases.desc:
Whether through sickness with the strife of the Hostility Phase or deft escalation during the Conciliation Phase, the Compromise Phase represents a growing accommodation between the peoples of Iberia. Differences fall by the wayside and shared history and heritage binds former foes together.

The peninsula stands at a cross-roads: if conflicts reappear, then the Opportunity Phase awaits.

The product of a notable Compromise Phase, during this Phase, relations between the peoples of Iberia grow so cordial that outsiders find their permissiveness difficult to parse. Inter-Faith Marriages are particularly common.

This can't last forever, though, and abuses of trust will eventually bring the Iberian Struggle back around to the Compromise Phase.

desc:
The Iranian Intermezzo depicts the tumultuous decline of the Abbasid Caliphate, in which Mesopotamia was ravaged by rebellions and power struggles and several Persian rulers asserted their independence.

Though Involved Characters can have many agendas, most will want to either become a Supporter of Caliphal Authority and work towards restoring the power of the Caliphate, or a Detractor of the Caliphate and try to destroy it.

The Struggle shifts between two Phases - Unrest and Stabilization.
name: Iranian Intermezzo

phases.desc:
Despite the brewing troubles, the caliph still commands respect. Rebellions and factionalism are on the back foot, but the lords of Persia will not be brought easily to heel.

The tension might spiral into Unrest, which would mean more chaos to come.
